title: Unescaped quotes in onclick strings took the whole app down
symptom: On the deployed site no tab rendered and every nav click was dead. The page looked fine; nothing worked.
root_cause: Five onclick handlers were built as JS strings containing unescaped single quotes inside single-quoted string literals. That is a parse error, and a parse error anywhere in an inline script kills the entire script, not the one handler.
detection: Reported from the live site after deploy.
fix: Escape the quotes, and make the build parse every inline script with node before it will write a page.
guard: build.py node-parses every inline script and fails the build on a syntax error
lesson: Generated code is code. If your build writes JavaScript into a string, the build must parse the result, because the blast radius of one bad character is the whole file, not the line.
cost: a live outage of the trainer

title: School URLs vanished from the sitemap when the data file was split
symptom: Per-school pages were live and correct, and absent from sitemap.xml.
root_cause: The sitemap generator read schools.json. When the library was split into one file per school, nothing read the new directory, and a loop over an empty list emits nothing rather than failing.
detection: Noticed while reviewing the built sitemap.
fix: Generate sitemap entries from the same directory scan the pages are built from.
guard: the build asserts the sitemap URL count matches the page count
lesson: A refactor that moves data has to be followed to every reader, and a loop over nothing is the quietest failure in programming. Derive counts from one source and assert they agree.
cost: unknown period of missing indexation

title: Item banks were different on every build because Python randomises hash()
symptom: Two builds of the same commit produced different banks, and the per-section bias figures pinned in the test file drifted run to run.
root_cause: build_banks.py seeded each category with abs(hash(exam + skill)). Python randomises string hashing per process by default.
detection: A pinned test figure would not stay pinned.
fix: Seed from zlib.crc32, which is stable across processes.
guard: three consecutive builds must produce identical output
lesson: Any generator that claims reproducibility must be seeded from something stable across processes. hash() is not, in Python, and the failure shows up as a flaky test rather than as a wrong answer.
cost: a flaky ratchet that would have been disabled eventually

title: A shadowed variable silently deleted 3000 items
symptom: ACT Maths dropped from 4500 items to 1500 and the build reported success.
root_cause: Adding an ACT English mapping declared a second ACT_MAP that shadowed the existing one. Nothing errors when a map is smaller than it used to be.
detection: Comparing the reported category counts against the previous build.
fix: Merge the maps properly and read the section per skill.
guard: the build prints per-category counts and the test file pins them
lesson: Deletion by shadowing is invisible. Any collection whose size is a fact about the product needs its size asserted, not just its contents.
cost: 3000 items, caught before merge

title: The adaptive engine was learning from nobody
symptom: The attempts table held zero rows in production while the app was plainly being used.
root_cause: Cloud.logAttempt returns early without a signed-in user, and the product deliberately requires no account. So the one path that recorded answers was the one path most users never took.
detection: Querying the production table and finding it empty.
fix: item_events: an unlinkable telemetry table with no user, session, device or address column, which is exactly why it needs no consent gate.
guard: smoke_consent asserts the telemetry body carries no identifying field
lesson: Check that your instrumentation fired at all before you trust anything built on it. An empty table looks identical to a quiet week.
cost: weeks of telemetry never recorded

title: Sentence equivalence items were unanswerable however well you answered
symptom: Every GRE sentence equivalence item graded as wrong.
root_cause: The items carry a two-element key and the engine graded by requiring an array of two, but answerInputs had no branch for that type, so they rendered as single pick and returned a scalar.
detection: Rendering and grading one item of every schema.
fix: Add the missing input branch.
guard: smoke_items renders and grades one item from all 182 generator schemas at phone width
lesson: A type system spread across a renderer and a grader will drift. The cheapest guard is one that exercises every variant end to end, once.
cost: eleven items unusable since they shipped

title: The dedup key counted a reshuffled question as a new one
symptom: Bank counts were inflated. The same question with its options rearranged looked distinct.
root_cause: canon() hashed the choices in the order they appeared, while the answer's position is randomised per draw.
detection: Sorting the choices before hashing, which immediately collapsed the counts.
fix: Sort the choices inside canon().
guard: canon() sorts, and the build reports distinct counts per category
lesson: A deduplication key must be canonical under every transformation the item legitimately undergoes. Ask what varies per draw before you hash.
cost: four ACT categories reported far above their real size

title: Four passages produced five hundred fake distinct questions
symptom: A reading generator with four passages reported five hundred distinct stated-idea items.
root_cause: The identity of a reading item is the passage plus the question asked, not the choices offered. The same stem with the same key varied only in which distractors came along.
detection: Reading the generated output rather than its count.
fix: canon() lets a generator declare that its identity is the passage plus the question.
guard: per-category distinct counts printed at build time
lesson: The same inflation arrives through a different door every time you close one. When you fix a dedup bug, ask what else shares an identity.
cost: would have shipped a bank five hundred deep and four questions wide

title: Two conditionals hashed identically and half the inference items would have vanished
symptom: Half of a passage's inference questions disappeared from the corpus.
root_cause: Both conditionals produced the stem 'which of the following can be properly inferred from the passage', so they hashed to the same value and one was dropped as a duplicate.
detection: Measuring true yield per passage.
fix: Each conditional names the case it asks about.
guard: yield per passage is measured and recorded, not assumed
lesson: Dedup can be wrong in both directions. An over-broad key deletes real content as silently as a narrow one inflates it.
cost: half the inference items in any corpus

title: CSS comments do not nest, and one placeholder killed the palette on 1451 pages
symptom: The colour palette was gone from every college page. It looked like a design problem and was chased as one for hours.
root_cause: A `{{CHROME_CSS}}` placeholder was left inside an opening CSS comment in rankings_base.css. The first */ closes the outer comment, so everything after it was live CSS that overwrote the palette.
detection: Eventually, by reading the built CSS rather than the template.
fix: Remove the nested comment.
lesson: CSS comments do not nest. When a whole page category loses its styling, read the built artefact, not the source that produced it.
cost: hours, on 1451 pages

title: A length guard silently dropped sixteen valid items
symptom: Sixteen items never appeared in the bank.
root_cause: The guard measured characters, and the items were legitimately longer than the limit in characters while being normal in content.
detection: Counting inputs against outputs.
fix: Measure what the guard actually cares about.
guard: input and output counts are compared at every filter stage
lesson: Every filter needs its rejection count reported. A filter that silently drops is indistinguishable from an input that was never there.
cost: sixteen items

title: Postgres fired triggers alphabetically and revoked every adult opt-in
symptom: Legitimate adult opt-ins to the data sharing programme were silently revoked.
root_cause: Postgres fires same-timing triggers in alphabetical order by name. profiles_sharing_eligibility sorted before profiles_sync_age_tier, so eligibility was judged against a stale age tier.
detection: Testing the guarantee the triggers were supposed to provide, rather than reading the trigger code.
fix: Numeric prefixes on trigger names to force the order.
guard: src/sql smoke tests assert the guarantee, not the implementation
lesson: Postgres fires same-timing triggers alphabetically. If two triggers on one table have an order dependency, encode it in the name, and test the outcome rather than the code.
cost: every adult opt-in, silently

title: UPDATE OF fires on the columns named in the statement, not the ones that changed
symptom: Updating birth_year stored a minor's tier and skipped the eligibility check entirely.
root_cause: UPDATE OF <columns> keys off the columns named in the UPDATE statement, not off what actually changed and not off what an earlier BEFORE trigger wrote into NEW.
detection: Same guarantee test as INC-0012.
fix: Fire on every update and compare OLD to NEW inside the function.
guard: sharing eligibility fires on every update
lesson: UPDATE OF is a statement-shape filter, not a change filter. If you need 'when this value changed', compare OLD and NEW yourself.
cost: a minor could pass the adult gate

title: A hardcoded count in the meta description went stale, and Google showed it
symptom: The meta description claimed 1,451 colleges after the number changed. og:description and twitter:description both derive from that tag, so all three were wrong.
root_cause: A figure typed into a template instead of computed at build time, which is the exact failure build-time counting exists to prevent.
detection: Reading the built page.
fix: Derive the number from the same count the pages are built from.
guard: no hardcoded corpus counts in templates
lesson: Any number in user-facing copy that describes the size of something must be computed from that thing at build time. The moment it is typed, it has a half-life.
cost: a wrong figure in the search result snippet

title: The whole bank blocked first paint: 20 seconds to the first question on 3G
symptom: On throttled regular 3G, 20.3 seconds to the first GMAT question and 23.4 for ACT.
root_cause: The entire item bank shipped as a blocking script. It grew past ten megabytes without anyone measuring what that cost.
detection: A throttled measurement, added because the number had never been taken.
fix: A strided starter bank plus an async remainder that pushes into the same array. ACT 7.6s, GMAT 11.0s; blocking download 11.3MB to 1.2MB.
guard: smoke_load measures time to first question under throttling
lesson: Nobody notices a page getting slower one commit at a time. Put the number in a test the first time you care about it, not the first time somebody complains.
cost: every visitor on a slow connection, for weeks

title: The performance test waited for the load event, which waits for the thing being optimised
symptom: A change that made the page usable nine times faster would have reported no improvement.
root_cause: smoke_load waited for the load event. The load event waits for the async bank, which is precisely the part the fix moved off the critical path.
detection: The number refused to move when it obviously should have.
fix: Wait for the first question to be answerable.
guard: smoke_load waits on the user-visible milestone
lesson: Measure the moment the user can act, not a browser lifecycle event. A test that measures the wrong instant is worse than no test, because it produces a number people trust.
cost: would have hidden the entire win

title: A build guard silently narrowed its own scope when the counts grew
symptom: The item-count guard kept passing while checking nothing.
root_cause: The guard matched \d{2,4}. When the banks passed ten thousand, the two largest counts stopped matching the pattern and fell out of the check.
detection: Reading the guard while raising the counts.
fix: Match any run of digits.
guard: the guard asserts how many counts it checked
lesson: A regex with a length bound is a guard with an expiry date. Assert the number of things checked, not only that the checks passed.
cost: the two largest banks unchecked

title: The Do Not Sell button was invisible from the day it shipped
symptom: White text on a transparent background on a white page. A legally required control that nobody could see.
root_cause: The page referenced nine colour custom properties that exist nowhere. CSS does not treat an undefined custom property as an error; it falls back to the initial value and paints.
detection: An automated contrast audit across every page.
fix: Define the tokens and fix seven contrast failures, all site wide because all lived in shared chrome.
guard: weekly_audit checks computed contrast on every page
lesson: An undefined CSS custom property is silent. Audit computed colour, not authored colour, and do it on the rendered page.
cost: an invisible compliance control for the life of the page

title: The audit reported a working link as broken
symptom: A false positive in the launch audit.
root_cause: Relative link resolution in the audit did not match the browser's.
detection: Checking a reported failure by hand.
fix: Resolve links the way the browser does.
lesson: Check your checker. A tool that cries wolf gets muted, and then it is worse than nothing.
cost: trust in the audit

title: Revoking EXECUTE from anon did nothing while PUBLIC still held it
symptom: Functions stayed callable after their grants were revoked from anon and authenticated.
root_cause: PUBLIC is a separate grantee. A leading =X/postgres in pg_proc.proacl means PUBLIC holds EXECUTE, and revoking from the named roles changes nothing.
detection: Re-running the Supabase advisors instead of trusting the per-role grants.
fix: Revoke from PUBLIC as well, everywhere.
guard: every migration revokes from public, anon, authenticated together
lesson: In Postgres, revoking from every role you can name still leaves PUBLIC. Verify with the advisors or by reading the acl, never by reading your own migration.
cost: an open function surface believed closed

title: A test passed because nothing was configured at all
symptom: smoke_funnel's 'nothing sent on refusal' assertion passed. It would have passed with the feature deleted.
root_cause: The test used storage key sfn_consent instead of sfn_consent_v1, so consent was never set up, so nothing was ever sent, so the assertion held vacuously.
detection: Fixing the key, which immediately exposed a real bug underneath.
fix: Use the real key, and assert the positive case as well as the negative.
guard: every 'nothing happens' assertion is paired with a 'something happens' assertion
lesson: A negative assertion passes when the system is broken in the right way. Always pair it with the positive case, or it is testing nothing.
cost: a real bug hidden behind a green check

title: A try/catch caught nothing because the call inside it does not throw
symptom: An error path never ran.
root_cause: The wrapped call signals failure by return value, not by throwing, so the catch was unreachable.
detection: A review bot playing a full exam against the real engine.
fix: Check the return value.
guard: review_bot.js sits each exam repeatedly against the real engine
lesson: try/catch around an API that returns errors is decoration. Know which convention each call uses before you wrap it.
cost: a silent failure path

title: www and the apex were two origins, so consent and rankings split in half
symptom: Two hostnames served the same site. localStorage is per origin, so a visitor who arrived on both had two consent states and their ranking signal was split.
root_cause: No canonical host redirect. The Cloudflare connector available here has no zone-level tools, so it had to be solved in the Worker.
detection: Reasoning about origin scoping while investigating traffic.
fix: src/worker.mjs 301s www to the apex, with run_worker_first true so the asset router does not answer first.
guard: smoke_redirect asserts the redirect and that run_worker_first stays true
lesson: Two hostnames are two origins and therefore two of everything the browser scopes by origin. Pick one and redirect on the server, not in a meta tag.
cost: split consent state and diluted ranking signal

title: The .git directory was being served on production
symptom: https://startfromnowhere.com/.git/config returned 200.
root_cause: .assetsignore excluded src/, data/ and supabase/ but not **/.git. Cloudflare's asset uploader walks the repository root, which is the assets directory.
detection: An adversarial review of the deploy exclusion list, after the first version of that list had already shipped.
fix: Exclude **/.git, and rewrite the guard to derive what must be served from real references rather than a hand-written allowlist.
guard: smoke_redirect derives the must-serve set with git check-ignore and asserts the source is excluded
lesson: An exclusion list is a denylist, and denylists are wrong by omission. Derive the allowed set from what the built pages actually reference.
cost: the full repository history publicly readable

title: A stale edge cache made a fixed 404 look like a live 200
symptom: After the fix deployed, /.git/config still returned 200.
root_cause: Cloudflare had cached the response with max-age=300. The fix was live; the verification was reading the cache.
detection: Re-requesting with a cache-busting query string, which returned 404.
fix: None needed in code.
lesson: Verify a cache-fronted fix with a cache-busting request, or you are testing the cache. This costs one query parameter and saves an hour of chasing a fix that already worked.
cost: minutes, and nearly a wrong conclusion

title: I reported a regression that was seed noise
symptom: I reported that SAT band coverage fell from 88 to 72 percent after an engine change.
root_cause: I compared a single seed before and after. Across seeds 3, 7 and 11 the baseline was 52, 88 and 80 against 72, 80 and 72 for the change. The spread between seeds was larger than the effect.
detection: Running more seeds because the number looked too clean.
fix: Report across seeds, never one.
guard: review_bot runs multiple seeds and reports the spread
lesson: A stochastic measurement on one seed is an anecdote. If your system has randomness, a single-run before-and-after cannot distinguish a change from the weather.
cost: a false regression report, corrected in the same session

title: A 29.88 MiB bank file would have failed the deploy the moment it merged
symptom: None yet. The build succeeded locally and the deploy would have rejected the file.
root_cause: Cloudflare Workers static assets cap a single file at 25 MiB. Raising the generated banks pushed the ACT rest-bank past it.
detection: Checking the platform limit against the real output size before pushing.
fix: Chunk the rest-bank at 18 MiB per file and glob the chunks in numeric order.
guard: the build fails on any asset over 25 MiB
lesson: Know your platform's hard limits and assert them in the build. A deploy-time rejection is a bad place to learn a number your build could have told you.
cost: would have broken the deploy

title: The service worker precache regex did not match the chunked files
symptom: Chunked bank files would not have been precached offline.
root_cause: The IMMUTABLE pattern was /bank_rest\.js$/, which does not match bank_rest1.js.
detection: Reading the service worker while changing the file naming.
fix: /bank_rest\d*\.js$/.
guard: smoke_offline asserts every bank chunk is precached
lesson: When you change a filename scheme, grep for the old name as a string, including inside regexes. A pattern is a hardcoded name wearing a disguise.
cost: offline would have silently degraded

title: A sequential colour ramp inverts direction between themes, and the label text did not
symptom: White heatmap labels on a light cell in dark mode.
root_cause: A sequential ramp runs light to dark in a light theme and dark to light in a dark theme. The label colour was hardcoded white, so it was correct in one theme and unreadable in the other.
detection: Rendering the chart in dark mode and looking at it.
fix: An --sfnc-on-seq token that flips with the theme.
guard: smoke_charts asserts token parity between the light and dark blocks
lesson: A dark mode does not break by having a wrong colour. It breaks by missing one. Any colour paired with a ramp has to move with the ramp.
cost: an unreadable chart in one theme

title: The theme parity test matched by name prefix and caught a font size
symptom: The parity guard flagged --text-xs, which is a length, not a colour.
root_cause: Token selection was by name prefix rather than by whether the value is a colour.
detection: Reading the failure.
fix: Select tokens by inspecting the value.
guard: smoke_charts selects by value, not name
lesson: Classify by what a thing is, not by what it is called. Naming conventions are a hint, never a type.
cost: a false failure

title: The browser suites had never actually run, because npm install had not
symptom: Browser tests appeared to be part of the suite and were not being executed.
root_cause: playwright was listed as a devDependency and node_modules did not exist in the environment.
detection: Running them by hand and getting a module-not-found.
fix: Add npm install and playwright install to CI, and check in package.json.
guard: CI runs npm run test:browser
lesson: A test that is not wired into CI is a test that does not exist. Prove a suite runs in the place it is supposed to run, not on your machine.
cost: an unknown number of regressions unnoticed

title: ARR was rounded to whole dollars and lost real money at small scale
symptom: $159.84 of ARR printed as $160.
root_cause: The currency formatter was called with zero decimal places for the larger tiles, a rule chosen for readability at scale and applied at a scale where cents still matter.
detection: A smoke test whose expected values were computed by hand before the page was written.
fix: Keep cents below a thousand dollars, drop them above.
guard: smoke_business asserts the exact printed figures
lesson: A fixed rounding rule is wrong at one end of the range or the other. Pick the precision from the magnitude, and write the expected number down before you write the code that produces it.
cost: a wrong figure on the tile the owner reads most closely

title: The dashboard test measured a hidden element and passed
symptom: Layout and contrast assertions passed on a view that was never displayed.
root_cause: The admin view carries a hidden class. A display:none element still answers innerText and getComputedStyle, so every assertion held on a box that had never been laid out.
detection: Screenshotting the result and seeing the dashboard was not in it.
fix: Call show('admin') and dismiss the onboarding overlay before measuring.
guard: smoke_business asserts the view is on screen and taller than 400px before measuring it
lesson: Before you measure a layout, assert the thing is rendered. Hidden elements answer most DOM questions, and they answer them wrongly.
cost: a layout suite that tested nothing, caught the same day

title: A line chart interpolated between discrete money events
symptom: A line drawn between $13.32 on the 18th and $4.99 on the 19th, passing through every value in between.
root_cause: Money movement was charted as a time series. A line encodes continuity, and these are discrete events on particular days.
detection: Rendering it and looking at it.
fix: Bars for movement and cash. Lines are reserved for measures that genuinely vary continuously.
lesson: Chart form is a claim about the data. A line claims the values in between existed. Ask whether that claim is true before choosing it.
cost: a chart that implied numbers that never happened

title: Two Stripe event types announce one new subscription
symptom: None: caught in design. Logging new subscriptions from both checkout.session.completed and customer.subscription.created would have doubled new MRR.
root_cause: Stripe announces a new subscription through both events, with different event ids, in no guaranteed order.
detection: Working out the idempotency key before writing the handler.
fix: A partial unique index on (source, subscription_id, kind) for the once-per-lifetime kinds, so the database decides rather than whichever event arrived first.
guard: billing_events_once_idx
lesson: Idempotency belongs in the database, not in the handler. Handlers race; unique indexes do not.
cost: would have doubled the headline revenue figure

title: charge.amount_refunded is cumulative, so partial refunds double-count
symptom: None: caught in design. A second partial refund reports the running total, which would have counted the first refund twice.
root_cause: Stripe's charge object reports total refunded to date, not the amount of this refund.
detection: Reading the field's semantics rather than its name.
fix: Use the most recent entry in the refunds list, falling back to the cumulative total for the ordinary single full refund.
lesson: Read what a payment field means, not what it is called. Cumulative and incremental fields look identical until the second event.
cost: would have overstated refunds

title: Cancellation erases the number you need to record the cancellation
symptom: None: caught in design. Churned MRR would always have been zero.
root_cause: The profile write on cancellation nulls plan_amount_cents and plan_interval. That row was the only place the departing subscriber's price still existed.
detection: Tracing the order of writes in the handler.
fix: Read the prior profile state before the cancellation write, and log what they were paying.
guard: priorState() is called before writeProfile in both the deleted and updated branches
lesson: When a write is destructive, capture what you need from the old value first. Ask what question you will want to answer after this row is gone.
cost: would have reported zero churn forever
